text:
Damon Severson is playing more than 22 minutes a night for Columbus and has only seven shots in 13 games. That's not a typo. Two of them went in, including a one-timer off a Zach Werenski feed in Dallas, so the 28.6% shooting is about as unrepeatable as it gets.

The points are lighter than the play. Columbus has 51% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, four points better than without him, and the team has scored 6.8 more goals than expected when he's out there. He has two points in his last ten games anyway.

He was much better than his reputation last season: Evolving-Hockey had him 20th among 215 defensemen in wins above replacement, driving play at one end (94th percentile) and suppressing it at the other (96th). Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him as a strong setup man. Our projection sees about 37 points. We'd like to see him shoot.
